trial_court: Family Court-II, Bhubaneswar, C.P. No.1031 of 2025
case_name: Dr. Amrita Mohanty vs Sandeep Kumar Mohanty
facts_of_case: The parties are seeking divorce on mutual consent and dissolution of marriage which was solemnized on 13.05.2013 at Bhubaneswar. They have remained separated for more than ten years and several litigations have been initiated against each other.

legal_principles.principle: While considering a petition U/s 13 B (2) of Hindu Marriage Act, the court should consider: (i) how long parties have been married?, (ii) how long litigation is pending?, (iii) how long they have been staying apart?, (iv) are there any other proceedings between the parties?, and (v) have the parties arrived at genuine settlement which takes care of alimony, custody of child or any other pending issues between the parties?
legal_principles.held: It has been settled by Hon'ble Apex Court in Amardeep Singh vs Harveen Kaur [2017 8 SCC 746]
cited_cases: Amardeep Singh vs Harveen Kaur, (2017) 8 SCC 746

legal_principles.principle: If there is no chance of reunion and there are chances of fresh rehabilitation, the court should not be powerless in enabling the parties to have better option.
legal_principles.held: It has been further held that if there is no chance of reunion and there are chances of fresh rehabilitation, the court should not be powerless in enabling the parties to have better option.
cited_cases: Amardeep Singh vs Harveen Kaur, (2017) 8 SCC 746

use_for_drafting: advising on joint application for divorce
